raw_events_note: Raw OpenCode event streams and the full inside-scratch observations file are not published. Only sha256 digests and byte counts are retained. Host boot ids and process ids are omitted from this summary.
scope: Sequential parent-exit-before-child-continuation only. No host-reboot, terminal-hangup, or simultaneous-death survival claim. The fixture agents performed marker/acknowledgement work only: no registration, data download, evaluation, submission, wallet, campaign, or nested-agent action. The only memory evidence is session history; one raw todowrite event was found post-run but is not reconciled with the recorded unknown native-task field, so native goal/task semantics stay unknown.

parent.role: fresh parent CLI process (no resume flag)

child.role: distinct fresh child CLI process; later resumed only by its own session id

invocations.note: Placeholders replace host paths. The external bridge invoked the scheduler executor; OpenCode itself ships no native scheduler.

recorded_field.reason: no native task/todo tool event was observable in this harness

native_task_tool_events.raw_stream_note: Raw-stream inspection at publication time found one actual todowrite tool event in the preserved child-bootstrap stream: it created a native task item titled lifecycle-fixture (status pending). The recorded observations field above still says unknown, so this summary does not silently overwrite it; native goal/task/todo semantics remain unreconciled and the capability stays conservative. The raw stream itself is not published.

memory.note: Both acknowledgements reported the same one-time marker that existed only in the child's first prompt/session history, so the recall is session-history evidence only. The recorded observation reports no native task/todo event; raw-stream inspection found one todowrite creation (see native_task_tool_events), which is not reconciled and does not upgrade this capability.

paused_tick.note: Pause control is scoped to the external bridge's queued marker dispatch; this is not evidence that arbitrary active native OpenCode work can be paused.

stopped_tick.note: Stop control is scoped to the external bridge's queued marker dispatch; terminal triggers stayed stopped in the bounded post-stop window. This is not evidence about arbitrary active native OpenCode work.

separately_labeled_inert_regression.result: passed: 19 lifecycle checks behaved as expected with inert fixture processes only
separately_labeled_inert_regression.note: Inert controls never prove native OpenCode crash or pause behavior and are kept separate from the actual native observation above.
